table_title: For each of the five best-selling lifetime game consoles (per Wikipedia's `List of best-selling game consoles` master article: PlayStation 2 / Nintendo Switch / Nintendo DS / Game Boy & Game Boy Color / PlayStation 4, ranked DESC by lifetime units sold, top 5 selected), list the three best-selling titles with units sold (millions) and release year. Title scope inherits per-console list articles' definitions — for Game Boy & Game Boy Color partition, the top 3 includes grouped-generation entries (Pokémon Generation I, Pokémon Generation II) per the source's own ranking convention; documented in normalization_decisions. Master accessed 2026-05-18; per-console pages carry heterogeneous source-specific sales-data dating.
db_analog: SELECT c.console, t.title, t.units_sold_millions, t.release_year FROM titles t JOIN consoles c ON t.console = c.console WHERE c.console IN (SELECT console FROM consoles ORDER BY lifetime_units_sold DESC LIMIT 5) AND t.rank_within_console <= 3 ORDER BY c.lifetime_units_sold_rank ASC, t.units_sold_millions DESC, t.release_year ASC
temporal_note: Master accessed 2026-05-18. 6 registered sources (1 console master + 5 per-console list pages); each per-console list page carries its own source-specific sales-data dating, which is heterogeneous across partitions and not collapsed into a single global as-of: Nintendo Switch list `as of March 31, 2026`; Nintendo DS list `as of March 31, 2025`; Game Boy & Game Boy Color list last edited 2026-05-18 with per-row date variation; PlayStation 2 + PlayStation 4 lists do not state a uniform global as-of, with per-row figure dates spread across 2018-2023 (PS4) and the platform's commercial lifetime (PS2). temporal_sensitivity = medium because (a) consoles whose commercial life has ended (PS2, DS, Game Boy/Color) have stable sales tallies; (b) Nintendo Switch is still selling so its top-3 rankings may shift slightly over multi-year horizons; (c) PS4 sales-data dating is heterogeneous within the staged top-3 figures. Console partition scope: top 5 consoles by lifetime units sold per master ranking (PS2 160M / Switch 155.92M / DS 154.02M / Game Boy & Color 118.69M / PS4 117.2M). Next console below cut: PlayStation [PS1] at 102.49M then Wii at 101.63M — wide 117.2M-vs-102.49M boundary at the rank-5 cut. Per-row Units Sold (millions) cells are NORMALIZED from heterogeneous source forms — the source presents figures variably as '71.08 million' (Switch table) / '45,900,000' (Game Boy table with comma-grouped integer) / 'over 35 million copies of Tetris were shipped worldwide' (Game Boy Tetris row, text-with-disclaimer); staged cells are mechanical normalization to numeric millions with one-decimal precision. Title cells are verbatim from each per-console list page, including grouped-generation entries (Pokémon Generation I + Pokémon Generation II in the Game Boy & Game Boy Color partition) — these are the source's own ranked top-3 entries and not a curator-substitution for single-game rows. Title cell wording chosen over 'Game' to honestly reflect this. Sort = master-console-ranking order primary (partition order: PS2 → Switch → DS → Game Boy & Color → PS4); within-partition Units Sold (millions) DESC; Release Year ASC tiebreak (not triggered at staged top-3 values — all within-partition Units Sold values are distinct). The deterministic-universe-rule preference is satisfied: master scope picks top-5 by units sold; each partition's top-3 is the per-console list's source-ranked head.
_extraction_notes: Hierarchical_decomposition instance — top-K-per-partition pattern (top 3 titles per top 5 lifetime consoles = 15 rows). Same operation_type=projection pattern as `top_5_highest_mountains_per_continent` (top-K-per-continent precedent) and `three_brightest_stars_in_each_zodiac_constellation` (top-K-per-constellation precedent). PIVOT from `top_5_oldest_universities_per_continent` after that candidate hit a WebFetch tool truncation on the master article that made source-faithful staging infeasible — the universities-pivot reasoning is documented in the prior cycle-1 design-review comments.json trail. The video-games candidate uses bounded per-console list pages which fetched reliably across all 5 partitions during cycle-0 source exploration. Brings `hierarchical_decomposition` from gap-1 (4 of 5) to **SATURATED at 5/5** — 11th fully-cleared category (alongside factual_lookup 6/5, top_k 6/5, multi_hop 5/5, qualitative 6/5, multi_attribute_projection 8/8, set_operation 8/8, set_filter 5/5, causal 5/5, implicit_join 9/8, scaled_enumeration 6/5). Culture/Gaming EXISTING subdomain (Culture family) per audit-cycle-1 amendment #1 — the repo already classifies the existing video-games instance under Culture/Gaming (per domain_taxonomy.md:38 and instance_selection_priorities.md:1750); reuses the existing subdomain rather than inventing a Technology/Gaming sibling for the same answer entity. Culture/Gaming extends from 1 (`trial_union_5`) to 2 instances. NEW Culture/Gaming subdomain is NOT introduced — joining existing fine-class. artifacts/video-games EXISTING fine-class (held by `trial_union_5`) — this instance is a 2nd video-games-keyed staged instance, NOT a NEW fine-class. Schema: 4 cols (Console + Title composite PK + Units Sold (millions) + Release Year) per audit-cycle-1 amendment #3 — Publisher column dropped because the PS2 + PS1 pages contain region-specific publisher cells (worldwide Rockstar + Japan Capcom) in top rows; cleaner first-pass schema avoids multi-publisher normalization complexity. Per audit-cycle-1 amendments: (1) N=5 not 6 (drops PS1 at 102.49M; the 117.2M-vs-102.49M boundary between rank-5 PS4 and rank-6 PS1 is wide, vs the narrower 102.49M-vs-101.63M between rank-6 PS1 and rank-7 Wii — N=5 is the cleaner cut); (2) source_count=6 not 1 (master defines partition universe but each per-console page supplies its partition's ranked row set + value cells — same pattern as zodiac-stars); (3) Title (not Game) wording in ID/columns/question to honestly cover grouped-generation entries (Pokémon Generation I/II); (4) Publisher dropped; (5) ID renamed `_titles_per_top_5_lifetime_consoles` (Title wording + N=5 explicit); (6) normalization note on Game Boy + Game Boy Color combined partition with grouped-generation top rows. Per-question recommendations applied: (Q1) N=5; (Q2) Game Boy + Game Boy Color combined; (Q3) source_count=6; (Q4) Units Sold normalized to numeric millions; (Q5) artifact accessed 2026-05-18 + preserve source-specific sales dating heterogeneously; (Q6) disputed figures use list page's primary displayed number with footnoted-caveat documentation; (Q7) PlayStation = master-verbatim (the original/PS1 console — not staged in N=5 universe); (Q8) Publisher dropped; (Q9) Release Year = integer extraction from full release date; (Q10) operation_type = projection per local precedent; (Q11) artifacts/video-games existing fine-class; (Q12) tool friendliness verified across all 5 per-console fetches.
